docs.text: First Stars and First Galaxies Workshop 2026 Dates December 8 (Tue) – 10 (Thu), 2026 Venue Inamori Hall, Inamori Foundation Memorial Building, Ito Campus, Kyushu University, Fukuoka, Japan ( Access ; No. 52 on the Campus Map ) 744 Motooka, Nishi-ku, Fukuoka 819-0395, Japan About the Workshop This annual meeting has been held for approximately two decades to review recent progress and discuss future directions in the formation and evolution of objects in the early Universe. The topics have expanded with the development of the field and include: Formation and evolution of Population III and metal-poor stars First galaxies and high-redshift galaxies Cosmic reionization Formation and growth of massive black holes High-redshift AGNs and Little Red Dots High-redshift transients Star-cluster formation and hub-filament systems Galactic archaeology and gravitational-wave sources Until now, this meeting has mainly served as a domestic workshop in Japan, typically attracting 50-60 in-person participants. Beginning this year, we hope to broaden participation from neighboring countries and regions and gradually develop wider international exchanges. We therefore plan to conduct talks in English wherever possible. Some student presentations may be given in Japanese. We warmly welcome researchers and students interested in these topics, including students and early-career researchers who are new to the field. Invited speakers (tentative) Ke-Jung (Ken) Chen (ASIAA): The First Stars, Binaries, and Supernovae Myoungwon Jeon (Kyung Hee University): First stars and first galaxies Jongwon Park (Kyung Hee University): First stars Takayuki R. Saitoh (Kobe University): First galaxies Takashi J. Moriya (NAOJ): High-redshift transients Takahiro Morishita (Tohoku University): Observations of early galaxies Yoshito Shimajiri (Kyushu Kyoritsu University): Hub-filament systems Organizers Doris Arzoumanian (Kyushu University), Ataru Tanikawa (Fukui Prefectural University), Kazuyuki Omukai (Tohoku University), Tomoya Kinugawa (Shinshu University), Kazuyuki Sugimura (Hokkaido University), Nozomu Tominaga (NAOJ), Shingo Hirano (Kanagawa University), Hajime Fukushima (University of Tsukuba), Takashi Hosokawa (Kyoto University), Masahiro Machida (Kyushu University), Naoki Yoshida (The University of Tokyo) Acknowledgments Contact Hajime Fukushima (University of Tsukuba): fukushima_at_ccs.tsukuba.ac.jp

docs.text: Links Past Workshops First Stars and First Galaxies Workshops (in Japanese) Venue Access to Ito Campus Getting to Ito Campus (PDF) Ito Campus Map (PDF) — Inamori Hall is in the Inamori Center, No. 52 Getting to the Venue From Fukuoka Airport At Fukuoka Airport (Fukuokakuko) Station (K13) on the Fukuoka City Subway Airport Line, take a train bound for Chikuzen-Maebaru (筑前前原) or Nishi-Karatsu (西唐津) . These trains continue directly onto the JR Chikuhi Line. If your train terminates at Meinohama (姪浜), change there to a JR Chikuhi Line train. Get off at Kyudai-Gakkentoshi (九大学研都市) Station (about 30 minutes from the airport). Take a Showa Bus bound for Kyudai Ito Campus (九大伊都キャンパス) and get off at Kyudai Rigakubu / School of Science (九大理学部) (about 15 minutes). The Inamori Center is directly in front of the bus stop. Arriving at the international terminal? Take the free shuttle bus to the domestic terminal (about 10 minutes), where the subway station is located. From Hakata or Tenjin Hakata (K11) and Tenjin (K08) are on the same subway line. Take a train bound for Chikuzen-Maebaru or Nishi-Karatsu and follow steps 2–3 above. Nishitetsu buses also run directly from Hakata Station and Tenjin to Ito Campus (about 50 minutes). Taxis are also available at Kyudai-Gakkentoshi Station. Fukuoka City Subway Route Map Accommodation Most hotels are located in the Tenjin and Hakata areas, which have direct train access to Kyudai-Gakkentoshi Station. Please allow about one hour from these areas to the venue, including the bus ride. A limited number of hotels are available closer to the campus, around Kyudai-Gakkentoshi and Meinohama Stations. We recommend booking early.
